Consult Summary:
- Young adult with known asthma presenting with 3 hours of acute chest tightness, wheeze, cough and mild exertional shortness of breath after a recent upper respiratory infection; treated remotely with inhaler prescriptions, oral steroid course, spacer and self-care advice.

History:
- Presenting complaint: acute chest tightness and wheeze for ~3 hours.
- Onset/duration/progression: symptoms began ~3 hours prior to consult; preceded by a cold/URTI last week; cough has persisted.
- Associated symptoms: wheeze, non-productive cough, mild shortness of breath (worse on exertion/stairs, not at rest), prior sore throat and runny nose that are improving.
- Pertinent negatives: no chest pain (described as tightness rather than pain), not coughing up sputum, not short of breath at rest.
- Past medical history: asthma (since childhood; prior severe exacerbation requiring hospitalization/intubation at ~16–17 years), hay fever/allergic rhinitis, childhood eczema, childhood milk protein allergy.
- Allergies: no known drug allergies (reports environmental/dust allergies).
- Current medications: previously used salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler and Clenil Modulite (inhaled steroid) — patient reports he ran out about one week ago and does not have them with him currently. (Conflict noted — later statement in transcript that he is “doing pretty good, just on the Clenil and the Salbutamol.”)
- Social/preventive care: university student; no other social history or immunization/smoking status documented.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: not documented.

Impression:
- Acute asthma exacerbation/wheeze triggered by recent upper respiratory infection.

Plan:
- Assessment summary: probable asthma exacerbation related to recent URTI; patient not acutely short of breath at rest and stable for outpatient management per remote assessment.
- Medications/prescriptions to be sent:
  - Salbutamol (Ventolin) inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.
  - Clenil Modulite (inhaled steroid) — dose/route/frequency not documented in transcript.
  - Oral steroid tablets prescribed — medication name not documented; instructed regimen: two tablets in the morning for five days (tablet strength/name not specified).
  - Spacer device to be provided with instructions.
- Self-management and safety advice:
  - Use Clenil in the morning; use Ventolin as needed for wheeze.
  - If using Ventolin more than every 3 hours or if symptoms worsen (increasing shortness of breath, chest pain/tightness, light-headedness), seek medical attention promptly.
  - Rest and consider time off work; patient may self-certify for first 7 days.
  - Read medication labels for steroid side effects; brief verbal counseling provided.
- Logistics/follow-up:
  - Prescriptions to be sent (doctor stated within approximately one hour).
  - No formal follow-up appointment documented; advised to seek care if deterioration.

document_quality / Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Objective assessment: vital signs (heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation), physical exam findings, and peak expiratory flow were not documented or measured.
  - Exact medication details: names/strengths of oral steroid and doses (mg) not documented; inhaler dose/strength and administration frequency not specified.
  - Smoking status, current immunization status (e.g., influenza), and detailed medication reconciliation.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Patient initially states he ran out of inhalers and does not have them with him; later states “I’m doing pretty good, just on the Clenil and the Salbutamol.” Conflict noted regarding current possession/use of inhalers.
- Transcript quality:
  - Overall intelligible; occasional brief audio dropouts/cutting in and out noted during parts of the consultation.
